newsitem.title: GERMANY: German May M3 boosted by stronger lending - Buba.
newsitem.headline: German May M3 boosted by stronger lending - Buba.

text.p: German M3 money supply growth accelerated in May, with the Bundesbank's key policy indicator expanding at a seasonally-adjusted, annualised rate of 7.0 percent from the fourth quarter of 1996 compared with 6.7 percent growth in April, the bank said on Friday.
The May growth confounded market expectations for a slowdown to between 6.0 and 6.5 percent and means that M3 remains above the Bundesbank's 1997 target growth corridor of 3.5 to 6.5 percent.
The Bundesbank said in a statement that M3 growth was boosted by a strengthening of lending to the private sector and by a weakening of money capital formation.
In addition, public sector borrowing from banks also grew in May, the Bundesbank said.
By contrast, high fund outflows abroad resulting from transactions by domestic non-banks helped dampen M3 growth, the Bundesbank said.
Non-annualised M3 in May grew 3.4 percent from the fourth quarter of 1996, up from 2.7 percent growth in April.
Compared with the fourth quarter of 1995, annualised M3 growth was 7.7 percent in May, unchanged from April.

The Bundesbank said the volume of sight deposits grew unusually strongly in May after having declined in April. Savings deposits with three months notice also expanded strongly, while short-term time deposits grew only moderately.
The Bundesbank also said its expanded M3 indicator, which comprises money market funds, grew only moderately in April, the most recent month for which data are available.
Annualised growth in expanded M3 for the six months November through April was seven percent, while standard M3 grew 6.5 percent over the period.
The Bundesbank also said that bank lending to the private sector was fuelled by a strong rise in short-term loans which was probably linked to strong money outflows abroad.
By contrast the growth of longer-term direct loans weakened.
